newsitem.title: UK: Dlr ends little changed in Europe as FOMC meets.
newsitem.headline: Dlr ends little changed in Europe as FOMC meets.

text.p: The dollar closed an uneventful European session barely changed as forex dealers stayed squarely focused on the outcome of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting.

Robust U.S. consumer confidence data for September provided more ammunition for the hawkish FOMC members to argue for a rate rise, analysts said. U.S. Treasuries fell on the strong report, but the dollar showed no marked response.
"This report clearly provides more evidence for the hawks to justify their call for a rate hike today," said Jeremy Hawkins, chief economic adviser at BankAmerica.
Consumer confidence was well above expectations at 118.8, compared with 107.00 forecast and 112.00 in August.
Dealers said the dollar's response to the FOMC meeting would depend on how the decision was explained to the market.
A rate hike sold as economic finetuning would soothe markets, while a poorly explained rise which suggested more tightening was in store would hit asset markets and the dollar.
Any announcement from the FOMC will be around 1815 GMT after European markets have closed.
The dollar was at 1.5124/28 marks and 109.70/75 yen by 1426 GMT compared with 1.5118/28 and 109.82/92 in late Europe Monday.
